title: Part 1: A Psychohistory of American Psychology:  The Sun and the Clock

sentences.en: Hi, this is Joel.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是乔尔。

sentences.en: Welcome to the Taproot Therapy Collective podcast, and this is part one of psychology itself on the couch, psychohistory of American psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听“直根疗法集体”播客，这是《心理学本身在诊疗椅上》系列的第一部分：美国心理学的心理史。

sentences.en: What psychology sees through American history, what it refuses to see, and why its relationship to what it can and can't let itself see changes over time.
sentences.zh: 心理学在美国历史上看到了什么，它拒绝看到什么，以及它与自身“能看”与“不能看”事物之间的关系为何随时间而改变。

sentences.en: There is a peculiar problem with eyes.
sentences.zh: 眼睛存在一个奇特的问题。

sentences.en: They can see everything in the world except themselves.
sentences.zh: 它们能看见世间万物，唯独看不见自己。

sentences.en: You can look at your hand, you can examine the texture of your skin, the lines on your palm, the way the light catches the fine hairs on your knuckles,
sentences.zh: 你可以看着自己的手，观察皮肤的纹理、掌心的线条，以及光线照在指关节细毛上的样子，

sentences.en: but you try and see your own eyes and the actual organs doing the seeing, and you encounter a fundamental impossibility.
sentences.zh: 但如果你试图看自己的眼睛，看那双正在进行观察的器官本身，你就会遇到一个根本性的不可能。

sentences.en: You can only look at reflection, you can only study photograph, but the thing that does the looking cannot look while itself is looking.
sentences.zh: 你只能看倒影，只能研究照片，但那个负责观察的东西，在它观察时是无法观察自身的。

sentences.en: Psychology is America's eye.
sentences.zh: 心理学就是美国的眼睛。

sentences.en: It's the apparatus through which we have learned to see ourselves.
sentences.zh: 它是我们学会审视自我的工具。

sentences.en: It provides the vocabulary that we use to describe our suffering.
sentences.zh: 它为我们描述痛苦提供了词汇。

sentences.en: It supplies the categories that we use to sort our experience, and it generates the explanations that we need for when we try to understand why we feel the way we feel.
sentences.zh: 它提供了我们整理经验的分类，并为我们试图理解为何会有某种感受时，提供了所需的解释。

sentences.en: For over a century, psychology has been the lens through which Americans have interpreted their inner life, and that is precisely why we cannot see it.
sentences.zh: 一个多世纪以来，心理学一直是美国人解读内心生活的透镜，而这正是我们无法看清它的原因。

sentences.en: We cannot see psychology because we are always looking through it.
sentences.zh: 我们看不见心理学，因为我们总是透过它在看世界。

sentences.en: Every time we try to examine it, we use the very concepts that it gave us.
sentences.zh: 每当我们试图审视它时，我们使用的正是它赋予我们的概念。

sentences.en: We inherit their limitations.
sentences.zh: 我们继承了它们的局限性。

sentences.en: When we critique the DSM using diagnostic thinking, we question therapy using therapeutic language.
sentences.zh: 当我们用诊断思维去批判《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）时，我们是在用治疗性的语言质疑治疗本身。

sentences.en: We deconstruct with the language of deconstruction.
sentences.zh: 我们用解构的语言进行解构。

sentences.en: We analyze the mental health system using its own framework, and the apparatus of examination is what's doing the examining.
sentences.zh: 我们用心理健康系统自身的框架去分析它，而进行审视的工具，正是那个被审视的对象。

sentences.en: This isn't really a metaphor, even.
sentences.zh: 这甚至算不上是一个比喻。

sentences.en: This is this defining epistemological trap of modern
sentences.zh: 这是现代美国意识中一种决定性的认识论陷阱，

sentences.en: American consciousness.
sentences.zh: 即美国人的意识。

sentences.en: Consider when you feel depressed, you probably describe it using words like symptoms and episodes.
sentences.zh: 想想看，当你感到抑郁时，你可能会用“症状”和“发作”之类的词来描述它。

sentences.en: And when you struggle with anxiety, you might wonder about your triggers or your attachment style.
sentences.zh: 当你为焦虑所困时，你可能会思考自己的“触发点”或“依恋类型”。

sentences.en: When relationships fail, you reach for concepts like boundaries or trauma response or cognitive distortion, and these words feel natural.
sentences.zh: 当人际关系破裂时，你会求助于“边界”、“创伤反应”或“认知扭曲”等概念，而这些词听起来很自然。

sentences.en: We don't know how to talk about ourselves without them.
sentences.zh: 没有它们，我们甚至不知道该如何谈论自己。

sentences.en: They feel accurate in describing reality, but they're not neutral observations.
sentences.zh: 它们在描述现实时感觉很准确，但它们并非中立的观察。

sentences.en: They're inheritance of specific historical choices made by specific people in specific circumstances.
sentences.zh: 它们是特定的人在特定的环境下，所做出的特定历史选择的遗产。

sentences.en: Choices that easily could have gone differently, hinge points that could have gone in a multitude of different
sentences.zh: 这些选择本可以轻易走向不同的方向，它们是历史中本可以通向无数种可能性的关键节点，

sentences.en: directions across history, and they still carry assumptions about the nature of human suffering that we've entirely forgotten to question.
sentences.zh: 而它们至今仍承载着关于人类痛苦本质的假设，我们却完全忘记了去质疑这些假设。

sentences.en: Psychology is America's blind spot because, not because we ignore it, but we're obsessed with it.
sentences.zh: 心理学是美国的盲点，不是因为我们忽视它，而是因为我们对它着了迷。

sentences.en: It is a blind spot because we have so thoroughly internalized its categories that we can no longer perceive them as categories at all.
sentences.zh: 它之所以成为盲点，是因为我们已经彻底内化了它的分类，以至于我们根本无法再将其视为分类。

sentences.en: We experience them as reality itself.
sentences.zh: 我们将它们视为现实本身。

sentences.en: This series is an attempt to step outside of that trap.
sentences.zh: 本系列节目旨在尝试走出这个陷阱。

sentences.en: Not by rejecting psychology, that would be impossible and foolish, but by understanding how it came to be, and by tracing the historical forces that shape its assumptions today.
sentences.zh: 不是通过拒绝心理学——那既不可能也不明智——而是通过了解它是如何形成的，并追溯那些塑造了它今日假设的历史力量。

sentences.en: By examining the question that it was designed to answer, and the questions that it was designed to make invisible.
sentences.zh: 通过审视它旨在回答的问题，以及它旨在使其隐形的问题。

sentences.en: Because here is the terrifying truth.
sentences.zh: 因为这里有一个可怕的事实。

sentences.en: Every American psychology has faced a crisis.
sentences.zh: 每一代美国心理学都面临过危机。

sentences.en: Every time the data has screamed that its assumptions were wrong, the profession has not responded by questioning those assumptions, but by doubling down on them.
sentences.zh: 每当数据大声疾呼其假设是错误的时候，这一行业做出的反应不是质疑这些假设，而是加倍坚持它们。

sentences.en: And we have built an entire system of psychological care on the foundations that even its architects knew were shaky, and sometimes when they intended it to be.
sentences.zh: 我们建立了一整套心理护理系统，其基础连它的缔造者都知道是摇摇欲坠的，有时甚至是有意为之。

sentences.en: And we've done so because the alternative, actually confronting what psychology
sentences.zh: 我们之所以这样做，是因为如果选择另一条路——真正去面对心理学所取代的东西及其原因——将要求我们审视美国计划中那些我们花了一个世纪去学习“视而不见”的部分。

sentences.en: replaced and why, would require us to look at parts of the American project that we have spent a century learning not to see.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: Psychology did not emerge to fill a natural void.
sentences.zh: 心理学的出现并非为了填补某种自然的空白。

sentences.en: It emerged to fill a void that was being actively created by forces much larger than itself, and it still is.
sentences.zh: 它的出现是为了填补一个由远比它自身更强大的力量所主动创造的空白，而且至今依然如此。

sentences.en: And it has spent the last hundred years trying to provide answers to questions that were never really about the mind at all.
sentences.zh: 过去一百年来，它一直试图为那些根本与心灵无关的问题提供答案。

sentences.en: And this is how the story happened.
sentences.zh: 故事就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: Part one, the world before the lens.
sentences.zh: 第一部分：透镜出现之前的世界。

sentences.en: To understand what psychology replaced, you have to understand what Americans used before psychology to make sense of their suffering.
sentences.zh: 要理解心理学取代了什么，你必须理解美国人在心理学出现之前，是如何解读他们的痛苦的。

sentences.en: But what
sentences.zh: 但那是什么呢？

sentences.en: was it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: What did they use to make sense of the world before psychology?
sentences.zh: 在心理学出现之前，他们用什么来解读世界？

sentences.en: What did they use to make sense of their suffering?
sentences.zh: 他们用什么来解读他们的痛苦？

sentences.en: The answer is almost everything else.
sentences.zh: 答案几乎是其他一切事物。

sentences.en: In 1890, the average American lived in a world with explanatory systeMs. If you felt despair, you might understand it as a spiritual trial, or a dark night
sentences.zh: 1890年，普通美国人生活在一个拥有解释系统的世界里。如果你感到绝望，你可能会将其理解为一种精神试炼，或灵魂的黑夜，

sentences.en: of the soul that would ultimately deepen your faith, something given to you for a reason.
sentences.zh: 它最终会加深你的信仰，这是某种有原因而赋予你的东西。

sentences.en: Even something meaningless was given meaning.
sentences.zh: 即使是毫无意义的事情，也被赋予了意义。

sentences.en: If you felt rage, you might channel it through your ethnic community's traditions of grievance and solidarity.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到愤怒，你可能会通过你所属族群的委屈与团结传统来宣泄它。

sentences.en: If you felt lost, you might locate yourself within your family's multi-generational story, your place in a chain of ancestors and descendants that gave your
sentences.zh: 如果你感到迷茫，你可能会在家族多代相传的故事中找到自己的位置，在祖先与后代的链条中找到自己的位置，这赋予了你

sentences.en: individual life cosmic significance.
sentences.zh: 个人生活以宇宙般的意义。

sentences.en: And that is if you were not brought here as an enslaved person who had no knowledge of where they came from and little memory of your family.
sentences.zh: 当然，前提是你不是作为奴隶被带到这里，对自己的出身一无所知，对家庭也几乎没有记忆。

sentences.en: If you felt exploited, you might understand that exploitation through the collective language of your trade union, your working class neighborhood, your fraternal organization.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到被剥削，你可能会通过工会、工人阶级社区或兄弟会的集体语言来理解这种剥削。

sentences.en: These were not primitive systems that psychology improved on.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是心理学所改进的原始系统。

sentences.en: They were sophisticated time-tested mechanisms, counterbalancing mechanisms for transforming raw suffering into meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们是复杂且经受过时间考验的机制，是用于将原始痛苦转化为意义的平衡机制。

sentences.en: And they shared one crucial characteristic.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有一个共同的关键特征。

sentences.en: They were communal.
sentences.zh: 它们是社区性的。

sentences.en: They located the individual within a web of relationships, obligations, and shared narrative that extended far beyond the boundaries of just the person.
sentences.zh: 它们将个人置于一张关系、义务和共享叙事的网中，这张网远远超出了个人的边界。

sentences.en: The church told you that your suffering was not random.
sentences.zh: 教会告诉你，你的痛苦并非随机。

sentences.en: It was part of a divine plan that connected you to every other suffering soul across time.
sentences.zh: 它是神圣计划的一部分，将你与跨越时空的每一个受苦的灵魂连接在一起。

sentences.en: The ethnic enclave told you that your struggles were the struggles of your people, inherited from ancestors and bequeathed to descendants.
sentences.zh: 族群聚居区告诉你，你的挣扎是你族人的挣扎，是从祖先那里继承并留给后代的。

sentences.en: And the union hall told you that your exhaustion and your poverty were not personal failures, but collective conditions that demanded collective solutions.
sentences.zh: 工会大厅告诉你，你的疲惫和贫困不是个人的失败，而是需要集体解决方案的集体状况。

sentences.en: Even in the saloon, you know, the place that was this sort of maligned cultural institution, it provided the space where men could process grief and rage and
sentences.zh: 即使是在酒馆里——你知道，那个被视为某种受诟病的文化机构的地方——它也提供了一个空间，让男人们可以在理解彼此的人的陪伴下，用被允许的语言处理悲伤、愤怒和

sentences.en: anger in the company of others who understood in a language that was allowed.
sentences.zh: 怨气。

sentences.en: And what all these systems had in common was that they pointed outward, they directed attention towards the social fabric, the community, or the shared condition.
sentences.zh: 所有这些系统的共同点在于，它们指向外部，将注意力引向社会结构、社区或共享的境遇。

sentences.en: And when something went wrong in your life, the first question was not, what is wrong with me, but what is happening to us?
sentences.zh: 当你的生活中出现问题时，第一个问题不是“我出了什么问题”，而是“我们发生了什么事？”

sentences.en: This nostalgia, you know, these systems were able to
sentences.zh: 这种怀旧感，你知道，这些系统能够

sentences.en: handle a tremendous amount of cruelty that the world was very good at dishing out.
sentences.zh: 处理这个世界非常擅长施加的巨大残酷。

sentences.en: And they enforced rigid conformity, but they also punished deviation.
sentences.zh: 它们强制执行严格的顺从，但也惩罚偏离。

sentences.en: They trapped people in roles that they never chose.
sentences.zh: 它们将人们困在他们从未选择的角色中。

sentences.en: The church could be authoritarian, the ethnic community could, could have an expectation, or a, you know, set of conditioning that was not fair.
sentences.zh: 教会可能是专制的，族群社区可能有一种期望，或者一套不公平的制约。

sentences.en: But, you know, what mattered was that when these structures broke down, when
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，重要的是，当这些结构崩溃时，当

sentences.en: immigration severed the connection to the old world, when industrialization destroyed the craft traditions, when
sentences.zh: 移民切断了与旧世界的联系，当工业化摧毁了手工艺传统，当

sentences.en: urbanization scattered the extended family, something had to fill that void, and humans cannot live without explanatory systeMs. We cannot endure, you know, suffering.
sentences.zh: 城市化分散了大家庭，必须有东西来填补这个空白，人类无法在没有解释系统的情况下生活。我们无法忍受，你知道，痛苦。

sentences.en: It means nothing.
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么都没有。

sentences.en: When the old framework crumbled, Americans did not simply become more rational, more scientific, more free, not even more religious.
sentences.zh: 当旧框架崩溃时，美国人并没有变得更理性、更科学、更自由，甚至没有变得更虔诚。

sentences.en: They became desperate for new ways to make sense of their life.
sentences.zh: 他们变得迫切需要新的方式来解读他们的生活。

sentences.en: Psychology did not create this crisis, but it did inherit it.
sentences.zh: 心理学并没有创造这场危机，但它确实继承了它。

sentences.en: To understand how the psychological metaphors of this era were changing, you have to understand that Americans were learning to think about energy differently.
sentences.zh: 要理解那个时代的心理学隐喻是如何变化的，你必须明白美国人正在学习以不同的方式思考“能量”。

sentences.en: By the late 19th century, energy meant steam.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪末，能量意味着蒸汽。

sentences.en: The locomotive had transformed the landscape, and the steam engine powered the factories.
sentences.zh: 火车头改变了地貌，蒸汽机驱动了工厂。

sentences.en: Thermodynamics, the science of heat, energy, and their transformation, was the master science of the era, explaining everything from the sun to the steam whistle.
sentences.zh: 热力学——关于热、能量及其转化的科学——是那个时代的统领科学，解释着从太阳到蒸汽汽笛的一切。

sentences.en: And when Americans began to think about the human mind, they reached for the metaphors that surrounded them.
sentences.zh: 当美国人开始思考人类心灵时，他们求助于周围的隐喻。

sentences.en: The mind was an engine.
sentences.zh: 心灵是一台引擎。

sentences.en: Emotions were pressures that built up and needed release.
sentences.zh: 情绪是积聚并需要释放的压力。

sentences.en: Repression was a boiler with a stuck valve.
sentences.zh: 压抑是一个阀门卡住的锅炉。

sentences.en: Neurosis was what happened when the pressure exceeded the system's capacity to contain it.
sentences.zh: 神经症是压力超过系统承受能力时发生的情况。

sentences.en: This was not merely a manner of speaking.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一种说话方式。

sentences.en: Sigmund Freud, who trained as a neurologist in an era when the nervous system was understood through hydraulic analogies, linked them to what he thought Americans were repressing.
sentences.zh: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，他在一个通过水力学类比来理解神经系统的时代接受了神经学训练，他将这些类比与他认为美国人正在压抑的东西联系起来。

sentences.en: The sexuality that was not allowed during his Victorian morality-coded time.
sentences.zh: 在他那维多利亚道德编码时代所不允许的性欲。

sentences.en: And he built his entire theoretical edifice on the language of pressure and discharge.
sentences.zh: 他建立了他整个理论大厦，用的就是压力和排放的语言。

sentences.en: The id contained primitive energies that demanded release.
sentences.zh: 本我（Id）包含着需要释放的原始能量。

sentences.en: The ego managed these pressures, channeling them into acceptable outlets.
sentences.zh: 自我（Ego）管理这些压力，将它们引导到可接受的出口。

sentences.en: Repression dammed the flow, but the pressure remained.
sentences.zh: 压抑阻断了流动，但压力依然存在。

sentences.en: And seeking any crack through which it could escape, it could make someone explode, enrage, or become psychotic and leaky.
sentences.zh: 它寻找任何可以逃逸的裂缝，这可能导致某人爆发、愤怒，或变得精神错乱、漏洞百出。

sentences.en: Blowing off steam was not just a phrase.
sentences.zh: “发泄”（Blowing off steam）不仅仅是一个短语。

sentences.en: It was a theory of psychological health.
sentences.zh: 它是一种心理健康理论。

sentences.en: And American psychology absorbed these metaphors because they made intuitive sense to a society obsessed with building literal engines that powered everything.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学吸收了这些隐喻，因为对于一个痴迷于建造驱动一切的实体引擎的社会来说，它们在直觉上是合理的。

sentences.en: The human being was a thermodynamic system.
sentences.zh: 人类是一个热力学系统。

sentences.en: Mental illness was an engineering problem.
sentences.zh: 精神疾病是一个工程问题。

sentences.en: Treatment meant adjusting the valves, releasing the pressures, and restoring the proper flow.
sentences.zh: 治疗意味着调整阀门、释放压力并恢复正常的流动。

sentences.en: And this was an improvement over some of the earlier frameworks.
sentences.zh: 这比早期的某些框架有所改进。

sentences.en: But it was certainly more scientific sounding than demonic possession or moral weakness.
sentences.zh: 而且它听起来确实比恶魔附身或道德软弱更科学。

sentences.en: And it carried with it assumptions that would shape American psychology for generations.
sentences.zh: 它随之携带的假设将塑造美国心理学数代人。

sentences.en: The human being was a machine.
sentences.zh: 人类是一台机器。

sentences.en: The mind operated according to mechanical laws.
sentences.zh: 心灵按照机械定律运作。

sentences.en: And the goal of treatment was to restore normal functioning to get the engine running smoothly again, which meant that someone had to understand each part of that engine.
sentences.zh: 治疗的目标是恢复正常功能，让引擎再次平稳运行，这意味着必须有人理解引擎的每一个部件。

sentences.en: They had to have a name.
sentences.zh: 它们必须有一个名字。

sentences.en: What this framework could not accommodate was the possibility that the engine was not really designed for the tracks that we were asking it to run on.
sentences.zh: 这个框架无法容纳的一种可能性是：引擎本身的设计可能并不适合我们要求它运行的轨道。

sentences.en: And that the pressures were building up, maybe not because the engine was malfunctioning, but because we were trying to run a train on a street instead of train tracks.
sentences.zh: 压力之所以积聚，可能不是因为引擎故障，而是因为我们试图在街道上而不是铁轨上开火车。

sentences.en: The machine was working.
sentences.zh: 机器本身在正常工作。

sentences.en: The world is what had broken.
sentences.zh: 坏掉的是这个世界。

sentences.en: Before the 1880s, Americans lived in local time.
sentences.zh: 1880年代之前，美国人生活在地方时间里。

sentences.en: Each town set clocks by the sun.
sentences.zh: 每个城镇根据太阳设定时钟。

sentences.en: When it was noon in
sentences.zh: 当波士顿是正午时，

sentences.en: Boston, it was not noon in New York or Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 纽约或费城还不是正午。

sentences.en: And this did not matter when the fastest thing moving was a horse.
sentences.zh: 当最快的交通工具是马匹时，这并不重要。

sentences.en: The railroad changed all that.
sentences.zh: 铁路改变了这一切。

sentences.en: A train traveling from New York to Chicago crossed dozens of local time zones, and schedules became impossible.
sentences.zh: 一列从纽约开往芝加哥的火车会穿过几十个地方时区，时刻表变得不可能实现。

sentences.en: Accidents occurred when engines sat on the track operated by different clocks.
sentences.zh: 当引擎停在由不同时钟操作的轨道上时，事故就会发生。

sentences.en: And in 1883, the railroads imposed standardized time zones on the entire continent.
sentences.zh: 1883年，铁路公司在整个大陆强制推行了标准化时区。

sentences.en: Local time was abolished, and the sun was dethroned.
sentences.zh: 地方时间被废除，太阳被拉下了王座。

sentences.en: The clock became the master.
sentences.zh: 时钟成为了主人。

sentences.en: And this seemed like a technical adjustment, but it was a revolution in the way that we made conscious experience.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是一次技术调整，但它是一场关于我们如何构建意识体验的革命。

sentences.en: For all of human history, people had lived by natural rhythm.
sentences.zh: 在整个人类历史上，人们一直按照自然节奏生活。

sentences.en: You woke with the sun, you worked while there was light, and the season shaped your labor.
sentences.zh: 你随太阳醒来，在有光时工作，季节塑造了你的劳动。

sentences.en: Your body knew when to be alert, and went to rest because your body had evolved over millions of years in synchrony with the turning of the earth.
sentences.zh: 你的身体知道何时警觉，何时休息，因为你的身体在数百万年的进化中与地球的自转保持同步。

sentences.en: And industrial time was different.
sentences.zh: 而工业时间则不同。

sentences.en: The factory whistle blew at 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 工厂汽笛在早上6点响起，

sentences.en: whether the sun was up or not, no matter what time of year it was.
sentences.zh: 不管太阳是否升起，也不管一年中的什么季节。

sentences.en: And the shift ended when the clock said it ended, not when the body said it was tired.
sentences.zh: 轮班在时钟说结束时结束，而不是在身体说累了时结束。

sentences.en: The assembly line moved at its own pace, and the worker adapted or was replaced.
sentences.zh: 流水线按自己的节奏移动，工人要么适应，要么被替换。

sentences.en: And time became a resource to be optimized, measured in minutes and seconds, and then bought and sold like any other commodity.
sentences.zh: 时间变成了一种需要优化的资源，以分秒计算，然后像任何其他商品一样被买卖。

sentences.en: And this reorganization of time required a radical redesign of our interior psychological space.
sentences.zh: 这种时间的重组需要对我们的内在心理空间进行彻底的重新设计。

sentences.en: The architecture of the early 20th century factory was explicitly engineered to facilitate total control over the production process, resulting in
sentences.zh: 20世纪初工厂的建筑结构被明确设计为促进对生产过程的全面控制，导致了

sentences.en: some of the first large-scale sensory deprivation and sensory overload experiments in American history.
sentences.zh: 美国历史上一些最早的大规模感官剥夺和感官过载实验。

sentences.en: In 1930, the Austin Company designed the first entirely windowless factory for the Simons Saw and Steel
sentences.zh: 1930年，奥斯汀公司为马萨诸塞州的西蒙斯锯钢公司设计了第一座完全没有窗户的工厂。

sentences.en: Company in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: By sealing the perimeter, the factory plunged workers into fully artificial lighting, severing their connection to the outside world, the weather, and the natural passage of the
sentences.zh: 通过密封周边，工厂将工人置于完全人工照明的环境中，切断了他们与外部世界、天气以及自然昼夜更替的联系。

sentences.en: day.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: Inside, the environment was dominated by deafening mechanical roars in a relentless assembly line speed, and this created a paradoxical psychological state.
sentences.zh: 在内部，环境被震耳欲聋的机械轰鸣声和无情的流水线速度所主导，这创造了一种矛盾的心理状态。

sentences.en: Simultaneous sensory deprivation from the lack of nature and sensory overload from the machines.
sentences.zh: 既有因缺乏自然而导致的感官剥夺，又有因机器而导致的感官过载。

sentences.en: The factory was a physical cage that required a complete rewiring of the nervous system to survive, and the psychological consequences were profound.
sentences.zh: 工厂是一个物理牢笼，为了生存，人必须彻底重塑自己的神经系统，其心理后果是深远的。

sentences.en: Rural Americans, whose ancestors had worked by the sun for generations, were being asked to reprogram their nervous system for machine time.
sentences.zh: 美国农村人祖祖辈辈日出而作，现在却被要求为机器时间重新编程他们的神经系统。

sentences.en: The bodies that showed up in the factories were not designed for this.
sentences.zh: 走进工厂的身体并非为此而设计。

sentences.en: They became fatigued, distracted, accident-prone.
sentences.zh: 他们变得疲惫、分心、容易出事故。

sentences.en: They resisted, and sometimes consciously.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了反抗，有时还是有意识的反抗。

sentences.en: Psychology entered this space as a technology of adaptation.
sentences.zh: 心理学作为一种适应技术进入了这个领域。

sentences.en: Its task was not to question whether the machine time was appropriate for human beings.
sentences.zh: 它的任务不是质疑机器时间是否适合人类。

sentences.en: Its task was to help human beings adjust to machine time, and the brass instruments in the psychology laboratories measured reaction times, attention spans,
sentences.zh: 它的任务是帮助人类适应机器时间，心理学实验室里的黄铜仪器测量着反应时间、注意力广度、

sentences.en: fatigue curves, all the variables that determined whether a worker could keep pace with a clock.
sentences.zh: 疲劳曲线，以及所有决定工人能否跟上时钟节奏的变量。

sentences.en: Behaviorism, which would soon dominate American psychology, was not just an academic theory.
sentences.zh: 行为主义很快将主导美国心理学，它不仅仅是一种学术理论。

sentences.en: It was a practical program for creating workers who could function in mechanical time, and if human
sentences.zh: 它是一项旨在创造能在机械时间下工作的工人的实践计划，如果人类

sentences.en: beings were simply stimulus response machines, then their inconvenient inner lives, their fatigue and
sentences.zh: 仅仅是刺激-反应机器，那么他们那些不便的内心生活、他们的疲劳和

sentences.en: their boredom and their longing for natural rhythms and especially meaning, could be trained away.
sentences.zh: 他们的厌倦，以及他们对自然节奏尤其是意义的渴望，都可以通过训练消除。

sentences.en: And the soul still remembered that the sun could overwrite this conditioning, and this was presented as science.
sentences.zh: 而灵魂依然记得太阳可以覆盖这种条件反射，这被当作科学呈现出来。

sentences.en: It was also, you know, whether its practitioners understood that or not, a service to the industrial order that was remaking American life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论从业者是否理解，这也是对正在重塑美国生活的工业秩序的一种服务。

sentences.en: In 1893, the World's Fair Columbian Exposition opened in Chicago, and millions of Americans passed through these gleaming pavilions marveling at the future that
sentences.zh: 1893年，芝加哥哥伦布纪念博览会开幕，数百万美国人穿梭于这些闪闪发光的展馆中，惊叹于技术所承诺的

sentences.en: technology promised.
sentences.zh: 未来。

sentences.en: And in the Anthropology Building, they encountered something strange, a psychology laboratory.
sentences.zh: 在人类学大楼里，他们遇到了一样奇怪的东西：心理学实验室。

sentences.en: The exposition featured gleaming brass instruments imported from the laboratories of
sentences.zh: 博览会展出了从德国莱比锡威廉·冯特（Wilhelm Wundt）实验室进口的闪亮黄铜仪器，

sentences.en: one Wilhelm Wundt in Leipzig, Germany, the man widely credited as the founder of experimental psychology.
sentences.zh: 他被广泛认为是实验心理学的奠基人。

sentences.en: Visitors marveled at the hip chronoscope, which could measure reaction times in milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 参观者惊叹于希普计时器（hip chronoscope），它能以毫秒为单位测量反应时间。

sentences.en: They examined the chymograph, which traced physiological responses on rotating druMs. They peered at the
sentences.zh: 他们观察着记录生理反应的转鼓记录仪（chymograph）。他们凝视着

sentences.en: aestheticometric, a compass designed to map the sensitivity of human skin.
sentences.zh: 美感测量仪（aestheticometric），这是一种旨在绘制人类皮肤敏感度的圆规。

sentences.en: The message was unmistakable.
sentences.zh: 传达的信息不言而喻。

sentences.en: The human mind was no longer a mystery.
sentences.zh: 人类心灵不再是一个谜。

sentences.en: It was an object, as immeasurable as a steam engine, as predictable as a chemical reaction.
sentences.zh: 它是一个物体，像蒸汽机一样可测量，像化学反应一样可预测。

sentences.en: And the soul had been replaced by the nervous system, and the nervous system could be timed, graphed, and quantified.
sentences.zh: 灵魂已被神经系统取代，而神经系统是可以计时、制图和量化的。

sentences.en: This was the moment when psychology announced itself to the American public.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学向美国公众宣告自己诞生的时刻。

sentences.en: Not as philosophy, and not as speculation, but as science.
sentences.zh: 不是作为哲学，也不是作为推测，而是作为科学。

sentences.en: Hard science.
sentences.zh: 硬科学。

sentences.en: Instrument science.
sentences.zh: 仪器科学。

sentences.en: The kind of science that built bridges and powered factories.
sentences.zh: 那种建造桥梁、驱动工厂的科学。

sentences.en: It was an audacious claim, and Wilhelm Wundt himself, back in his hometown, was far more cautious about what instruments could actually measure.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大胆的宣称，而威廉·冯特本人在回到家乡后，对仪器到底能测量什么要谨慎得多。

sentences.en: But he understood that the brass chronoscopes captured only the thinnest surface of mental life, reaction time, sensory thresholds, and the basic mechanics of perception.
sentences.zh: 但他明白，黄铜计时器捕捉到的只是心理生活最浅显的表面：反应时间、感官阈值以及感知的基本机制。

sentences.en: The deeper questions of consciousness, meaning, and human purpose remained untouched, but American psychology was in a hurry.
sentences.zh: 关于意识、意义和人类目的的更深层问题仍然未被触及，但美国心理学正急于求成。

sentences.en: It needed legitimacy, it needed funding, and it needed to prove that it belonged alongside physics and chemistry in the university, not regulated to the philosophy
sentences.zh: 它需要合法性，需要资金，它需要证明自己属于大学里的物理和化学系，而不是被降级到哲学系，

sentences.en: department where aging scholars debated unanswerable questions since ancient Greece.
sentences.zh: 在那里，年迈的学者们自古希腊以来一直在争论那些无法回答的问题。

sentences.en: And so it embraced the instruments, the measurements, the appearance of precision, even when that precision captured only
sentences.zh: 因此，它拥抱了仪器、测量和精确的外表，即使这种精确度只捕捉到了

sentences.en: a little bit of what actually mattered about the human mind.
sentences.zh: 人类心灵中真正重要的一小部分。

sentences.en: And this was the first instance of a pattern that would repeat throughout American psychological history.
sentences.zh: 这是美国心理学史上不断重复的一种模式的第一个实例。

sentences.en: The adoption of a scientific aesthetic as a substitute for scientific substance.
sentences.zh: 采用科学美学来替代科学实质。

sentences.en: The brass instruments looked like science, and they felt like science.
sentences.zh: 这些黄铜仪器看起来像科学，感觉也像科学。

sentences.en: They generated numbers that could be published in journals, but they could not answer the question of what actually tormented Americans in 1893.
sentences.zh: 它们产生的数据可以发表在期刊上，但它们无法回答1893年真正折磨美国人的问题。

sentences.en: Why do I feel so lost?
sentences.zh: 为什么我感到如此迷茫？

sentences.en: Why has the world betrayed me?
sentences.zh: 为什么世界背叛了我？

sentences.en: Why is the world of my parents gone?
sentences.zh: 为什么父母的世界消失了？

sentences.en: Why did my parents not prepare me for this one?
sentences.zh: 为什么父母没有让我为这个世界做好准备？

sentences.en: How do I make sense of a life that no longer follows the old rules?
sentences.zh: 我该如何理解一个不再遵循旧规则的生活？

sentences.en: And for those questions, Americans would need a different kind of psychological entity entirely.
sentences.zh: 对于这些问题，美国人需要一种完全不同的心理实体。

sentences.en: From such humble beginnings grew the astonishing modern world in which we now live.
sentences.zh: 从如此卑微的起点，成长为我们今天所处的惊人的现代世界。

sentences.en: We cannot conquer the mountains, but our railroads now run through them with ease.
sentences.zh: 我们无法征服大山，但我们的铁路现在可以轻松穿过它们。

sentences.en: We cannot defeat the river, but we can bend it to our will and damn it for our own purposes.
sentences.zh: 我们无法战胜河流，但我们可以让它屈从于我们的意志，并为了我们的目的筑坝拦截。

sentences.en: We now live in a time of endless possibility.
sentences.zh: 我们现在生活在一个充满无限可能的时代。

sentences.en: More has been learned about the treatment of the human body in the last five years than was learned in the previous 500.
sentences.zh: 过去五年里对人体治疗的了解比过去500年还要多。

sentences.en: 20 years ago, 39 was the number of years a man could expect from his life.
sentences.zh: 20年前，一个人预期的寿命是39岁。

sentences.en: Today, it is more than 47.
sentences.zh: 今天，这个数字超过了47岁。

sentences.en: Eventually, the train tunnels will crumble.
sentences.zh: 最终，火车隧道会崩塌。

sentences.en: The dams will be overrun.
sentences.zh: 大坝会被冲毁。

sentences.en: Our patients' hearts will all stop their beating.
sentences.zh: 我们病人的心脏终将停止跳动。

sentences.en: But we humans can get in a few good licks in battle before we surrender.
sentences.zh: 但在投降之前，我们人类可以在战斗中打出几记漂亮的重拳。

sentences.en: William James should have been the defining figure of
sentences.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯（William James）本应是美国心理学的

sentences.en: American psychology.
sentences.zh: 定义性人物。

sentences.en: He had every advantage, a Harvard professorship, a brilliant writing style, a philosophical range that encompassed everything from religion to neuroscience.
sentences.zh: 他拥有所有优势：哈佛教授职位、出色的写作风格、涵盖从宗教到神经科学的哲学广度。

sentences.en: His 1890 masterwork,
sentences.zh: 他1890年的杰作，

sentences.en: The Principles of Psychology, remains one of the most readable and human texts that the discipline ever produced.
sentences.zh: 《心理学原理》，至今仍是该学科产生过的最易读、最人性化的文本之一。

sentences.en: But James' vision of psychology was fundamentally incompatible with what America was becoming.
sentences.zh: 但詹姆斯的心理学愿景与美国正在变成的样子从根本上是不兼容的。

sentences.en: James believed that consciousness was a stream, coining the phrase stream of consciousness, continuous, flowing, ever-changing, impossible to chop into discrete measurable units.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯认为意识是一条河流，他创造了“意识流”这个词：连续、流动、不断变化，不可能被切割成离散的可测量单位。

sentences.en: More radically,
sentences.zh: 更激进的是，

sentences.en: James developed what he called radical empiricism, a philosophical position that insisted that the
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯发展了他所谓的“激进经验主义”，这是一种哲学立场，坚持认为

sentences.en: connections and meanings between things were just as real as the things themselves, even if they couldn't be measured.
sentences.zh: 事物之间的联系和意义与事物本身一样真实，即使它们无法被测量。

sentences.en: Fundamentally anti-scientific, because in science, if you can't measure it and know instruments are available to quantify it, then it can't be real.
sentences.zh: 这从根本上是反科学的，因为在科学中，如果你不能测量它，且没有仪器可以量化它，那么它就不可能是真实的。

sentences.en: Traditional science dealt with objects that could be isolated and measured.
sentences.zh: 传统科学处理的是可以被隔离和测量的对象。

sentences.en: And James argued that human experience was constituted precisely by the relationships that connected those objects.
sentences.zh: 而詹姆斯认为，人类经验恰恰是由连接这些对象的各种关系构成的。

sentences.en: You could not understand a person by breaking them into components any more than you could understand a melody by analyzing individual notes.
sentences.zh: 你无法通过将一个人拆解成各个部分来理解他，就像你无法通过分析单个音符来理解旋律一样。

sentences.en: James' psychology was expansive.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯的心理学是广阔的。

sentences.en: It included religious experience.
sentences.zh: 它包含了宗教体验。

sentences.en: It took seriously the testimony of mystics, about consciousness, and phenomenological states, transcendent states.
sentences.zh: 它认真对待神秘主义者关于意识、现象学状态和超验状态的证言。

sentences.en: It investigated mediums, telepathy.
sentences.zh: 它调查灵媒和心灵感应。

sentences.en: Not because James was incredulous, but because he believed science had no right to prematurely close any account of reality.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为詹姆斯轻信，而是因为他认为科学无权过早地关闭对现实的任何解释。

sentences.en: He wanted a field that was fundamentally open in a way that a purely objective, scientific, and quantifiable field cannot be.
sentences.zh: 他想要一个从根本上开放的领域，而这正是纯粹客观、科学和可量化的领域所无法做到的。

sentences.en: He was willing to sit with uncertainty, to hold open questions rather than forcing premature closure.
sentences.zh: 他愿意与不确定性共处，保持问题开放，而不是强行过早地得出结论。

sentences.en: And this is exactly why he could not be followed.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他无法被追随的原因。

sentences.en: America in 1900 was not interested in uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 1900年的美国对不确定性不感兴趣。

sentences.en: It was not interested in the flowing, ungraspable nature of consciousness, and it was not interested in anything other than a rigid system of control.
sentences.zh: 它对意识那种流动、难以捉摸的本质不感兴趣，除了僵化的控制系统外，它对任何事物都不感兴趣。

sentences.en: It was interested in prediction.
sentences.zh: 它感兴趣的是预测。

sentences.en: It was interested in taking the chaos of human behavior and rendering it manageable to fit into the society that it was building and the project that it was making.
sentences.zh: 它感兴趣的是将人类行为的混乱变得可管理，以适应它正在建设的社会和正在进行的工程。

sentences.en: James's colleague, James McKean Cattell, who had studied under Wilhelm Wundt in Germany, publicly attacked James.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯的同事詹姆斯·麦基恩·卡特尔（James McKean Cattell），曾在德国师从威廉·冯特，公开抨击了詹姆斯。

sentences.en: Cattell viewed psychology as a tool for generating applicable data that could be used in industry, government, to sort people to select workers to identify fit and unfit.
sentences.zh: 卡特尔将心理学视为一种工具，用于生成可应用于工业和政府的数据，以筛选人员、挑选工人、识别合格与不合格者。

sentences.en: And James' spiritualist tendencies, his openness to the unmeasurable, threatened that entire project.
sentences.zh: 而詹姆斯的唯灵论倾向，他对不可测量事物的开放态度，威胁到了整个计划。

sentences.en: Cattell wrote to
sentences.zh: 卡特尔写信给

sentences.en: James that his investigations into psychical research were doing much to injure psychology.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯，称他对心灵研究的调查正在严重损害心理学。

sentences.en: In the pages of the Journal of Science, Cattell warned his peers that they could not follow James into the quagmires of subjectivity.
sentences.zh: 在《科学杂志》的版面上，卡特尔警告同行，他们不能跟随詹姆斯陷入主观性的泥潭。

sentences.en: The reaction of William James was not a scientific necessity, it was a structural imperative.
sentences.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯的遭遇并非科学上的必然，而是一种结构性的强制。

sentences.en: And American institutions were beginning to demand a psychology that could deliver quantifiable results, test scores, efficiency metrics, sorting mechanisMs. James's psychology
sentences.zh: 美国机构开始要求一种能够提供可量化结果、考试分数、效率指标和分类机制的心理学。詹姆斯的心理学

sentences.en: of the stream, of radical connection, of irreducible meaning, simply could not be made to serve those purposes.
sentences.zh: 关于意识流、激进联系和不可还原意义的心理学，根本无法服务于这些目的。

sentences.en: This was a similar fallout that would happen between Freud and Jung on another continent, as we
sentences.zh: 这与我们在另一个大陆上弗洛伊德和荣格之间发生的冲突类似，正如我们

sentences.en: discussed in the Weird History of Psychotherapy series that we released on this podcast earlier.
sentences.zh: 在这个播客之前发布的《心理治疗的怪异历史》系列中所讨论的那样。

sentences.en: And it's because of all of these reasons that the father of American psychology was effectively orphaned by his own discipline.
sentences.zh: 正是因为所有这些原因，美国心理学之父实际上被他自己的学科遗弃了。

sentences.en: His influence would persist underground, resurfacing decades later in humanistic psychology
sentences.zh: 他的影响力将在地下持续存在，几十年后在人本主义心理学中重新浮现，

sentences.zh: 但剥夺普通美国人灵魂的阴谋并非在秘密金库中策划的。

sentences.en: It was walking right out in the open, clipboard in hand, being timed into a fraction of a second with a stopwatch on the factory floor.
sentences.zh: 它就在光天化日之下进行，拿着剪贴板，在工厂车间里用秒表精确到几分之一秒。

sentences.en: Everyone was participating in it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都参与其中。

sentences.en: And while Americans were looking for a monstrous system that was being turned on somewhere in the
sentences.zh: 当美国人在外部世界的某个地方寻找一个正在启动的怪物系统时，

sentences.en: external world, what they were feeling was actually a system on the interior of the self that was being desensitized, dissociated and turned off.
sentences.zh: 他们真正感受到的是一个正在自我内部启动的系统，它正在变得麻木、解离并被关闭。

sentences.en: One that would have monstrous consequences for the future of
sentences.zh: 这将对美国心理学的未来产生

sentences.en: American psychology.
sentences.zh: 可怕的后果。

sentences.en: I, I had really thought that I was incapable of this kind of behavior.
sentences.zh: 我，我真的以为自己没有能力做出这种行为。

sentences.en: I, I was surprised, you know, I was dismayed to find out that I could, I could really be a,
sentences.zh: 我，我很惊讶，你知道，我很沮丧地发现我竟然能，我真的能，

sentences.en: that I, that I could, uh, act in a, uh, manner.
sentences.zh: 我能，呃，以一种，呃，方式行事。

sentences.en: So, and I, and while I was doing it, I, uh, this was a part of me I hadn't really noticed before.
sentences.zh: 所以，我，当我在做这件事的时候，我，呃，这是我以前从未真正注意到的自己的一部分。

sentences.en: In 1913, a 35 year old psychologist named John B.
sentences.zh: 1913年，一位35岁的心理学家名叫约翰·B·

sentences.en: Watson delivered a lecture at Columbia University that would transform American psychology forever.
sentences.zh: 华生在哥伦比亚大学发表了一场演讲，这场演讲将永远改变美国心理学。

sentences.en: It became known as the behaviorist manifesto.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“行为主义宣言”。

sentences.en: Watson looked at the philosophical debates over consciousness, the careful distinctions between
sentences.zh: 华生审视了关于意识的哲学辩论，关于感觉与知觉之间细致的区分，

sentences.en: sensation and perception, the elaborate theories of introspection and the endless argumentation about the nature of the mind.
sentences.zh: 复杂的内省理论，以及关于心灵本质的无休止争论。

sentences.en: And he declared them all irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 他宣布这一切都无关紧要。

sentences.en: Psychology as the behaviorist views it, Watson announced, is a purely objective experimental branch of natural science.
sentences.zh: 华生宣布，行为主义者眼中的心理学是一门纯粹客观的自然科学实验分支。

sentences.en: Its theoretical goal is the prediction and control of behavior.
sentences.zh: 其理论目标是预测和控制行为。

sentences.en: Note the phrase prediction and control, not understanding, not healing, not describing, not even finding causation.
sentences.zh: 注意“预测和控制”这个词，不是理解，不是治愈，不是描述，甚至不是寻找因果关系。

sentences.en: The purpose of psychology was to predict what humans would do and control when humans did it.
sentences.zh: 心理学的目的就是预测人类会做什么，并控制人类何时去做。

sentences.en: Everything else was mystical speculation unworthy of science.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都是不值得科学研究的神秘推测。

sentences.en: In one stroke, Watson declared the stream of consciousness to be scientifically irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 华生一举宣布意识流在科学上是无关紧要的。

sentences.en: William James is flowing, meaningful, irreducible subjective experience off the table, the soul, the self, the inner depths that the philosophers had contemplated for millennia,
sentences.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯那流动、有意义、不可还原的主观体验被排除在外，灵魂、自我、哲学家们思考了千年的内心深处，

sentences.en: all eliminated and removed from the American project.
sentences.zh: 全部从美国计划中被消除和移除。

sentences.en: What remained was a human being as a biological machine, an input and output device that could be programmed by manipulating its environment.
sentences.zh: 剩下的只是作为生物机器的人类，一个可以通过操纵环境来编程的输入输出设备。

sentences.en: There was no need to understand what people felt or thought.
sentences.zh: 没有必要去理解人们感受或思考什么。

sentences.en: You only needed to know what stimuli produced the correct response.
sentences.zh: 你只需要知道什么刺激能产生正确的反应。

sentences.en: If humans were simply stimulus and response machines, then Taylor's stopwatch was the appropriate tool to study them.
sentences.zh: 如果人类仅仅是刺激和反应机器，那么泰勒的秒表就是研究他们的合适工具。

sentences.en: And if consciousness was irrelevant, then Ford's melting pot was a simply effective form of conditioning.
sentences.zh: 如果意识无关紧要，那么福特的大熔炉就是一种简单有效的条件反射形式。

sentences.en: If behavior could be predicted and controlled, then the skilled workers' troublesome autonomy was not a right to be respected, but a variable to be managed.
sentences.zh: 如果行为可以被预测和控制，那么熟练工人的麻烦自主权就不是一种需要尊重的权利，而是一个需要管理的变量。

sentences.en: And behaviorism was not imposed on American psychology by evil conspirators.
sentences.zh: 而且行为主义并非由邪恶的阴谋家强加给美国心理学。

sentences.en: It was succeeded because it fit.
sentences.zh: 它之所以成功，是因为它合适。

sentences.en: And it answered the questions that American institutions were asking.
sentences.zh: 它回答了美国机构当时正在提出的问题。

sentences.en: It provided a framework that made the emerging industrial order feel not just economically efficient, but scientifically inevitable.
sentences.zh: 它提供了一个框架，使新兴的工业秩序不仅在经济上显得高效，而且在科学上显得不可避免。

sentences.en: And that is perhaps the cruelest irony.
sentences.zh: 这也许是最残酷的讽刺。

sentences.en: Watson genuinely believed that he was being progressive.
sentences.zh: 华生真诚地认为自己是在追求进步。

sentences.en: In an era dominated by racism and eugenics, which argued that immigrants and minorities were genetically inferior, Watson's environmentalism
sentences.zh: 在一个种族主义和优生学盛行的时代，人们认为移民和少数族裔在基因上是低劣的，而华生的环境决定论

sentences.en: suggested that anyone could be molded into a productive citizen.
sentences.zh: 暗示任何人都可以被塑造成一个多产的公民。

sentences.en: It was the birth of a neoliberal order, or what would become one.
sentences.zh: 这是新自由主义秩序的诞生，或者说即将成为这种秩序。

sentences.en: And at the same time that the mind was being saved by, from, you know, racists, by the creation of a system that would allow anybody to change given the right stimuli,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当心灵通过创造一个允许任何人在给予正确刺激下都能改变的系统，从而从种族主义者手中被“拯救”时，

sentences.en: the same new instruments that were being used to study psychology were also being used to rewire it.
sentences.zh: 用于研究心理学的同样的新工具，也被用来重塑它。

sentences.en: The telegraph had already accomplished something unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 电报已经完成了一项前所未有的成就。

sentences.en: It separated information from transport.
sentences.zh: 它将信息与运输分离开来。

sentences.en: For all of prior human history, a message could only travel as fast as a human body could carry it.
sentences.zh: 在之前的所有人类历史中，消息的传播速度只能等同于人类身体的移动速度。

sentences.en: But the telegraph annihilated this constraint.
sentences.zh: 但电报消除了这一限制。

sentences.en: News from across the continent arrived within minutes.
sentences.zh: 来自大陆另一端的新闻在几分钟内就能到达。

sentences.en: The stock ticker brought Wall Street into offices everywhere.
sentences.zh: 股票行情自动收录机将华尔街带到了各处的办公室。

sentences.en: And time itself was standardized.
sentences.zh: 时间本身也被标准化了。

sentences.en: Not for philosophical reasons, but because the railroads needed coordinated schedules and the telegraph made coordination possible.
sentences.zh: 不是出于哲学原因，而是因为铁路需要协调的时间表，而电报使这种协调成为可能。

sentences.en: This was not merely a convenience, it was the reorganization of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一种便利，这是对意识的重组。

sentences.en: First the sun, then the clock, and now the beginning of the network.
sentences.zh: 先是太阳，然后是时钟，现在是网络的开端。

sentences.en: In the old world, information was generally tied to context where it could be acted upon.
sentences.zh: 在旧世界，信息通常与可以采取行动的语境相关联。

sentences.en: You learned about events in your community, your trade, your family, contexts where the information could guide decision and response.
sentences.zh: 你了解社区、行业、家庭中的事件，这些语境下的信息可以指导决策和反应。

sentences.en: The telegraph flooded Americans with information from everywhere, most of which they could do nothing about.
sentences.zh: 电报用来自各地的信息淹没了美国人，而其中大部分信息他们都无能为力。

sentences.en: The newspaper became a catalog of distant events, fascinating and disturbing and utterly disconnected from the reader's capacity to respond.
sentences.zh: 报纸变成了一份遥远事件的目录，令人着迷又不安，且与读者做出反应的能力完全脱节。

sentences.en: It was a flood of information.
sentences.zh: 这是一场信息的洪水。

sentences.en: And the result was a new kind of consciousness, informed but impotent, stimulated but also passive, aware of more than any previous
sentences.zh: 结果产生了一种新型的意识：知情但无力，受刺激但被动，比以往任何

sentences.en: generation and with less agency than any generation before them.
sentences.zh: 一代人知道的更多，但能动性却比他们之前的任何一代人都要少。

sentences.en: This was the consciousness that psychology would be asked to explain and manage.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学被要求去解释和管理的意识。

sentences.en: A nervous system that now extended across continents, not just families and small communities.
sentences.zh: 一个现在延伸到整个大陆，而不仅仅是家庭和小社区的神经系统。

sentences.en: All overwhelmed by inputs that it could not process, seeking frameworks to make sense of a world that no longer cohered.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都被无法处理的输入所淹没，寻求框架来理解一个不再连贯的世界。

sentences.en: The motion picture added another dimension.
sentences.zh: 电影增加了另一个维度。

sentences.en: By 1910, Americans were gathering in darkened theaters to watch flickering images of people who were not really
sentences.zh: 到1910年，美国人聚集在黑暗的剧院里，观看那些并不真正

sentences.en: there, in places that they had never been, doing things that they could never do, or maybe would never do.
sentences.zh: 存在的人的闪烁影像，在他们从未去过的地方，做着他们永远无法做，或者可能永远不会做的事情。

sentences.en: A heightened form of spectacle and experience that went beyond paintings and print magazines.
sentences.zh: 这是一种超越了绘画和印刷杂志的更高形式的奇观和体验。

sentences.en: This was not storytelling as humanity had always known it.
sentences.zh: 这不再是人类一直以来所熟知的讲故事方式。

sentences.en: Embodied, present, and communal, this was something new, a mass dream projected onto a screen, experienced simultaneously by millions, creating shared
sentences.zh: 具体、在场且具有公共性，这是一种新事物，一个投射在屏幕上的大众梦境，被数百万人同时体验，创造出共享的

sentences.en: references and shared desires that no organic origin in the community had created.
sentences.zh: 参考和共享的欲望，而这些欲望在社区中并无有机的起源。

sentences.en: William James, still writing in the last years of the 19th century, had insisted that consciousness was a stream, continuous, flowing, and unified.
sentences.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯在19世纪的最后几年仍在写作，他坚持认为意识是一条流，连续、流动且统一。

sentences.en: But that stream was being broken into disconnected pools, each reflecting a different facet of an increasingly incoherent world.
sentences.zh: 但那条流正在被分割成互不相连的水潭，每一个都反映着一个日益支离破碎的世界的不同侧面。

sentences.en: Psychology emerged in this environment, not as a neutral science of the mind, but as one technology among others, competing with the telegraph, the telephone,
sentences.zh: 心理学在这种环境下应运而生，它不是一门中立的心灵科学，而是众多技术中的一种，与电报、电话

sentences.en: and cinema to try and define what American self could become.
sentences.zh: 和电影竞争，试图定义美国人的自我可以变成什么样。

sentences.en: In 1920, Watson's academic career came to an end.
sentences.zh: 1920年，华生的学术生涯走到了尽头。

sentences.en: He was forced to resign from the John Hopkins University after his affair with a graduate student became public.
sentences.zh: 在与一名研究生的婚外情曝光后，他被迫从约翰·霍普金斯大学辞职。

sentences.en: What happened next tells you everything about the real purpose of behaviorist psychology.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情告诉你关于行为主义心理学真正目的的一切。

sentences.en: Exiled from academia, Watson did not disappear.
sentences.zh: 被学术界放逐后，华生并没有消失。

sentences.en: He joined the J.
sentences.zh: 他加入了J.

sentences.en: Walter Thompson advertising agency, one of the largest in the world.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特·汤普森广告公司，这是世界上最大的广告公司之一。

sentences.en: And within two years, he'd become vice president.
sentences.zh: 两年内，他就成为了副总裁。

sentences.en: He had realized that the same principles he used to study laboratory rats could be used to study and manipulate consumers.
sentences.zh: 他意识到，他用来研究实验室老鼠的同样原则，也可以用来研究和操纵消费者。

sentences.en: And before Watson, advertising was largely informational.
sentences.zh: 在华生之前，广告主要是信息性的。

sentences.en: It told you the virtues of a product, its price, its quality, its utility.
sentences.zh: 它告诉你产品的优点、价格、质量和用途。

sentences.en: Watson understood that human beings are not rational actors who evaluate products logically.
sentences.zh: 华生明白，人类不是逻辑评估产品的理性行为者。

sentences.en: He believed in an unconscious that previous advertisers had not, and they are biological machines responding to stimuli based on these unconscious processes.
sentences.zh: 他相信存在一种前人未曾察觉的潜意识，而人类不过是基于这些潜意识过程对刺激做出反应的生物机器。

sentences.en: He had no interest in understanding them, but he did have interest in manipulating them.
sentences.zh: 他无意去理解这些人，但他确实有兴趣操纵他们。

sentences.en: To sell products, you don't appeal to reason, you trigger reflexes.
sentences.zh: 为了推销产品，你不需要诉诸理性，而是要触发他们的条件反射。

sentences.en: While Taylorism controlled the worker's body during production, Ford's sociological department controlled the worker's social environment, and now Watson's advertising
sentences.zh: 泰勒制在生产过程中控制了工人的身体，福特的社会学部门控制了工人的社会环境，而现在，华生的广告学

sentences.en: controlled the worker's desires, ensuring that wages earned on the assembly line would flow back into the consumption of mass-produced goods.
sentences.zh: 控制了工人的欲望，确保他们在流水线上赚取的工资会回流到大众消费品中。

sentences.en: The loop was closed.
sentences.zh: 闭环完成了。

sentences.en: The human being, once embedded in communities of meaning, once possessed of craft knowledge and spiritual depth, once a citizen with the
sentences.zh: 人类曾经深植于意义共同体之中，曾经拥有工艺知识和精神深度，曾经是拥有

sentences.en: power to shape collective destiny, had been reconceptualized as a node in an economic circuit.
sentences.zh: 塑造集体命运权力的公民，如今却被重新定义为经济回路中的一个节点。

sentences.en: Stimulus in, response out, labor in, consumption out.
sentences.zh: 输入刺激，输出反应；输入劳动，输出消费。

sentences.en: Watson himself was remarkably explicit about what he had accomplished.
sentences.zh: 华生本人对自己所取得的成就直言不讳。

sentences.en: In 1924, he published his famous boast,
sentences.zh: 1924年，他发表了那段著名的豪言壮语：

sentences.en: Give me a dozen healthy infants, well-formed, and my own specified world to bring them up in,
sentences.zh: 给我一打健康的婴儿，身体健全，并给我一个由我指定的环境来抚养他们，

sentences.en: and I'll guarantee to take any one at random and train him to become any type of specialist I might select.
sentences.zh: 我保证能随机挑选出任何一个，并把他训练成我所选定的任何类型的专家。

sentences.en: Doctor, lawyer, artist, merchant chief, and yes, even beggar man and thief, regardless of his talents, penchants, tendencies, abilities, vocations, and race of his ancestors.
sentences.zh: 无论是医生、律师、艺术家、商界领袖，甚至是乞丐或小偷，无论他的天赋、爱好、倾向、能力、职业以及他祖先的种族如何。

sentences.en: Human agency had been erased, not by religious dogma, but by tyranny, by science, or at least the aesthetics of science.
sentences.zh: 人类的主体性被抹去了，不是被宗教教条，而是被暴政，被科学，或者至少是被科学的美学所抹去。

sentences.en: Looking back at the trajectory of American psychology from 1892 to the 1920s, the sheer scale of the transformation becomes terrifyingly clear.
sentences.zh: 回顾1892年到1920年代美国心理学的发展轨迹，这种转变的巨大规模变得令人恐惧地清晰。

sentences.en: In three decades, psychology had been enlisted to help solve a problem that it did not name, how to make human beings compatible with machines.
sentences.zh: 在三十年间，心理学被征召去解决一个它从未命名的问题：如何让人类与机器相兼容。

sentences.en: The steam engine had provided the metaphor, pressure, release, thermodynamic regulation.
sentences.zh: 蒸汽机提供了隐喻：压力、释放、热力学调节。

sentences.en: The telegraph and cinema had become the rewiring.
sentences.zh: 电报和电影则完成了重构。

sentences.en: Fragmented attention, information without action, and behaviorism had provided the theory, humans as input and output devices.
sentences.zh: 碎片化的注意力、无行动的信息，以及行为主义提供了理论：人类即输入和输出设备。

sentences.en: William James offered a vision of a humanity that was radical, pluralistic, and deeply connected to the profound mysteries of consciousness and experience.
sentences.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯提出了一种激进、多元且与意识和经验的深奥奥秘紧密相连的人性愿景。

sentences.en: Also, a self-evidencing principle that was internal, a subjective space that the behaviorists had no interest in.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个内在的自我证明原则，一个行为主义者毫无兴趣的主观空间。

sentences.en: James saw the individual as an active meaning-making agent in complex and interconnected nodes, where the spaces between the nodes were important.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯将个体视为复杂且相互关联的节点中积极的意义创造者，而节点之间的空间至关重要。

sentences.en: But this vision was fundamentally incompatible with a society transitioning to mass industrialization.
sentences.zh: 但这种愿景与一个正在向大规模工业化转型的社会根本不兼容。

sentences.en: The factory floor did not need meaning.
sentences.zh: 工厂车间不需要意义。

sentences.en: It needed compliance, and the system did not need souls, it needed hands.
sentences.zh: 它需要的是服从，系统不需要灵魂，它需要的是劳动力。

sentences.en: The ghosts of the 1920s still heavily haunt our present reality.
sentences.zh: 1920年代的幽灵至今仍沉重地萦绕在我们的现实生活中。

sentences.en: The digital algorithms that carefully curate your social media feeds, the biometric surveillance that monitors modern warehouses, and all of the people who work inside them.
sentences.zh: 精心策划你社交媒体信息流的数字算法，监控现代仓库的生物识别技术，以及所有在其中工作的人们。

sentences.en: These are all direct descendants of
sentences.zh: 这些都是华生的宣言和泰勒的秒表的直系后裔。

sentences.en: Watson's manifesto and Taylor's stopwatch.
sentences.zh: 华生的宣言和泰勒的秒表。

sentences.en: They are the refined, hyper-normalized iteration of a system explicitly designed to bypass our consciousness, erase our agency, and hijack our reflexes.
sentences.zh: 它们是一个系统的精致且高度常态化的迭代，该系统旨在绕过我们的意识，抹去我们的主体性，并劫持我们的条件反射。

sentences.en: And we see this today in the modern strategy of non-linear warfare, pioneered by Vladislav Storkov in Putin's Russia, one of his propaganda directors.
sentences.zh: 我们在当今的非线性战争战略中看到了这一点，这是普京俄罗斯的宣传主管之一弗拉迪斯拉夫·斯托尔科夫所开创的。
zh_words: 弗拉迪斯拉夫·斯托尔科夫

sentences.en: The goal of this modern psychological warfare is not to sell a single lie, but to make the environment so loud, so filled with contradictory noise, that nothing feels real.
sentences.zh: 这种现代心理战的目标不是兜售一个谎言，而是让环境变得如此嘈杂，充斥着相互矛盾的噪音，以至于一切都显得不再真实。
